title: Mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order 10
statement: Find as many mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order 10 as possible: Latin squares that, taken two at a time and superimposed, show each of the 100 ordered pairs of symbols exactly once. Two are known (Parker 1959; Bose, Shrikhande and Parker 1960); three would be new.
submission: Text file: K Latin squares of order 10 one after another, each 10 rows of 10 symbols 0..9 (or 1..10) separated by spaces or commas; blank lines between squares are allowed.
score: K, the number of mutually orthogonal Latin squares (larger is better)

best_known.source: two MOLS of order 10 are known (E. T. Parker 1959; Bose, Shrikhande and Parker 1960); OEIS A001438 notes that 'Parker and others conjecture that a(10) = 2'; read 9 Nov 2026

bound.source: nine MOLS of order 10 would give a projective plane of order 10, which does not exist (Lam, Thiel and Swiercz 1989)
